clue.text: New racer — one fit for a mechanic

indicators.note: new here means made afresh, so the letters of the words around it are rebuilt

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A new racing driver is introduced as someone well suited to work as a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges RACER, I (one) and FIT together into the answer; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, especially a military or naval mechanic.

clue.text: Expression of sorrow about Swift's last book

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: alas is a cry expressing grief

indicators.note: last here takes only the final letter of the word Swift's

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over the final volume written by Jonathan Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T, the last letter of 'Swift's', inside ALAS. The Swift of the surface is the satirist Jonathan Swift.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps, a kind of book.

clue.text: To many an old jazz fan, a lively composition

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
cat was swing-era slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: Older jazz lovers regard a certain piece as spirited music.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece full of rapid, brilliant passages.

clue.text: Aristocratic Athenian propping up marsh plant

indicators.note: in a down answer, what props something up sits beneath it, so these pieces come below the marsh

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
U is the label for upper-class usage
a native of Athens is a Greek

explanation.surface: A nobleman from Athens holds up a plant growing in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'propping up' is a down-clue signal: what props something up sits below it in the grid. 'Aristocratic' gives U, the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenugreek is a leguminous herb grown for its aromatic seeds.

clue.text: Testimonials which may be centralised

indicators.note: may be suggests the following letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: References for a candidate, perhaps gathered in one central place.
explanation.definitionFit: Credentials are letters or documents vouching for a person's qualifications.

clue.text: Sound range of eggs

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a range of houses or seats is a row

explanation.surface: A spread of eggs that is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' means a word heard: ROW (a range, as in a row of houses) is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs inside a female fish.

clue.text: Fanatical bishop at centre of attack

indicators.note: at centre of puts one piece in the middle of another

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A zealous bishop finds himself in the thick of an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at centre of' places B in the middle of RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid can mean extreme or fanatical in opinion, as in a rabid supporter.

clue.text: Uses abusive language in bars

definitions.meaning: to rail is to complain bitterly or scold
horizontal bars, as on a fence

explanation.surface: Someone swears at people while drinking in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: One word both means scolds vehemently and names a set of horizontal rods.

clue.text: Military leaders captured during tea in the old country

indicators.note: captured during puts the captive piece inside the other

parts.note: bohea is a black China tea

indicators.note: leaders takes the leading letters of the word Military

explanation.surface: Army chiefs were seized at teatime in their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured during' signals a container; 'leaders' takes the first two letters of 'Military'. Bohea is an old name for a black China tea; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a historic kingdom of central Europe, now part of Czechia.

clue.text: Put up duty list famous for causing an explosion?

indicators.note: put up in a down answer means written upwards, so the run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a rota lists who is on duty
noted means well known

explanation.surface: Someone posts a well-known roster, apparently to set off a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns the whole run ROTA NOTED backwards, a down-clue signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is a device used to set off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Authorize six-footers to .take quarters

parts.note: insects have six legs, and lice are insects
the compass points north, south and east are quarters

explanation.surface: Permission is given for lice to move into lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link; N, S and E are three of the four compass quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: To license is to grant official permission, the verb in American spelling.

clue.text: Descriptive word for English mine before the crash

indicators.note: before puts the pieces ahead of what follows

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: crash suggests the letters of the little word the are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An adjective used about an English colliery shortly before disaster struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' scrambles the little word 'the', and 'before' sets English and the mine ahead of it; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase expressing a characteristic quality.

clue.text: Spilt the beans about student jargon

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sang is ... for confessed or informed
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Someone told all about the private language of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SANG; 'sang' as 'confessed' is criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary peculiar to a group, much like jargon.

clue.text: His tax-collecting formerly discomfited cinemas

definitions.note: the definition points to a man whose job is gathering duty

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: discomfited means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax official once caused trouble for picture houses with his levies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discomfited' is the anagram signal. The definition is oblique: the answer is the man whose tax-collecting this was, so the whole clue reads as his story.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer collecting duty on goods, a tax collector of old.

clue.text: Sailor upholds biscuit as of exceptional quality

indicators.note: in a down answer, what holds something up sits beneath it, so this piece goes below

parts.note: a cracker is a thin crisp biscuit
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman praises a biscuit as outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upholds' is a down-clue signal: JACK supports CRACKER from below; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackerjack is informal for excellent, first-rate.

clue.text: Health resort's endless boom

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a boom is a spar, as on a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A spa town is enjoying a never-ending economic boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from SPAR. The 's is 'is', a link, and 'boom' is the nautical pole, not prosperity.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs visited for health cures.

clue.text: Vessel's function to keep order in Burma

indicators.note: to keep means holding something inside

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: order means arrange, so the letters of Burma are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A ship's job is to maintain law and order in Burma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is the anagram signal and 'to keep' the container. The 's is 'is', a link, and 'function' is the trigonometric kind, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a vessel able to travel underwater.

clue.text: One more heartless vagabond is too much

parts.note: an extra is one more than needed

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a vagrant is a wandering vagabond

explanation.surface: Another hard-hearted tramp is more than anyone can bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central R out of VAGRANT; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extravagant means exceeding reasonable limits, excessive.

clue.text: Consequences of a noisy spell at the end of March

indicators.note: a noisy spell suggests the words are rendered by voice, so a phrase is spoken to give the entry

parts.note: something at the end of March comes after March

explanation.surface: The damage left behind by a stormy period of weather in late March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy spell' says the phrase is spoken: AFTER MARCH, said quickly in a non-rhotic accent, comes close to the answer. 'of a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftermath means the results following an event, especially an unpleasant one.

clue.text: A sign of disapproval initially exposed this illegitimate trading

parts.note: a black mark is a note of censure against someone

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of exposed and this

explanation.surface: A scolding mark first revealed this unlawful trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes E and T from 'exposed this'.
explanation.definitionFit: The black market is illicit dealing in scarce or controlled goods.

clue.text: Dismay about soldiers' clothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to appal is to dismay
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Distress over the state of the troops' uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps, a common crossword source of 'soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is formal for garments, clothing.

clue.text: French for "chariot'"?

definitions.meaning: a French conjunction meaning for or because
a poetic or archaic word for a chariot

explanation.surface: A query whether a French word stands for a chariot.
explanation.definitionFit: The French conjunction meaning because is spelt the same as a literary word for a war chariot.

clue.text: Anxiety about container for a rifle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: Concern over what box to use for storing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'for a' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbine is a short light rifle, originally for cavalry.

clue.text: Praise cocktail containing favourite aperitif

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the other inside it
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of Praise are mixed up

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone compliments a mixed drink served with a preferred pre-dinner tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes the letters of 'Praise', and 'containing' sets the favourite inside them. The definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is something taken before a meal to stimulate hunger, as an aperitif is.

clue.text: Health-giving food?

parts.note: read as a food you raise while wishing someone good health, rather than a nourishing meal

explanation.definitionFit: Toast is grilled bread, and also a drink proposed to someone's health.

clue.text: Two rivers associated with the country

parts.note: R abbreviates river, and the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian
R abbreviates river, and the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: A pair of rivers linked to a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: General honour for an old doctor

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order

explanation.surface: A general receives a distinction meant for an elderly physician.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech is an archaic word for a physician, from their use of bloodsucking worms.

clue.text: Hostile incursions made by Dorians

indicators.note: made by suggests the letters of the following word are used to form something new

explanation.surface: Raids carried out by the ancient Dorian Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' rearranges DORIANS. The Dorians were an ancient Greek people said to have invaded Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile raids into enemy territory.

clue.text: Sound of weeping upset employer no end

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so the letters run in reverse
no end means losing the final letter

parts.note: a boss employs people

explanation.surface: A tearful noise is heard from an endlessly troubled boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims BOSS to BOS, and 'upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob is a convulsive gasp made when crying.

clue.text: Cupidity of one seizing a couple of states

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
VA and RI are abbreviations for Virginia and Rhode Island, two US states
VA and RI are abbreviations for Virginia and Rhode Island, two US states

explanation.surface: The greed of someone grabbing two territories at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' is the container signal; the two states are given by their US postal abbreviations. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed for wealth, and cupidity is an older word for greed.

clue.text: Striking effect recalled in an Oriental ceremony

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
in means the letters lie inside the phrase Oriental ceremony

explanation.surface: A dazzling moment remembered from an Eastern ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to TALCE spanning 'Oriental ceremony', and 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliant success or showy effect.

clue.text: Cooks when she is retained by hospital for a little money

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last piece follows on
is retained means held within, so the word she goes inside

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook in a hospital kitchen is kept on for a small tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is retained' puts the word 'she' inside the cooking word, and 'by' adds the hospital. Baksheesh is a tip or bribe, from Persian.
explanation.definitionFit: Baksheesh is a small gratuity or bribe, as given in parts of Asia.
